core/ai/local_infer.py - local GGUF inference via llama-cpp-python (lazy import).

This module is the **local** branch of the recipe-inference engine. It mirrors
``recipe_infer.infer_recipe`` but runs entirely offline against a user-supplied
GGUF model (no API key, no network).

llama-cpp-python IS bundled in the V.2.0.0 installer (spec uses collect_all and
drops the old excludes=['llama_cpp']). The import stays lazy so a missing engine
still raises a clear, actionable error instead of crashing at import time.

Four layered defences against the
"access violation reading 0x0000000000000000" crash
---------------------------------------------------
The crash is the ctypes surface for *any* exception raised inside the C log
callback registered by ``llama_cpp._logger`` at import time. We now block
every known trigger:

  1. ``sys.stdout`` / ``sys.stderr`` are None in a frozen windowed build.
     ``_ensure_stdio`` redirects them to utf-8 devnull.
  2. The default log callback does ``text.decode("utf-8")`` *before* writing.
     If the backend emits bytes that aren't valid UTF-8 (locale-formatted
     numbers, Windows error strings, etc.) this raises UnicodeDecodeError
     inside the C callback. ``_install_noop_log_callback`` replaces the
     default callback with a module-level no-op kept alive so ctypes cannot
     collect it.
  3. ``verbose=False`` swaps sys.stderr for ``llama_cpp._utils.errnull_file``
     which is opened at import time with the system default encoding (gbk on
     Chinese Windows). Even though the no-op callback swallows logs, we
     still patch these files to utf-8 as defence in depth
     (``_patch_llama_utils_utf8``).
  4. ``Llama(...)`` is always invoked with ``verbose=False`` to match the
     proven-working OfflineDocAI release (Jul 29).

The proven OfflineDocAI release avoids all of this because its model lives
under ``models/`` (ASCII path) and the default callback never sees non-ASCII.
We replicate that *and* harden it so Chinese paths in the model directory
also work.

本地推理引擎（llama-cpp-python）尚未打包进本程序。
请在开发环境执行 `py -3.11 -m pip install llama-cpp-python`，
并把 core.ai.local_infer 加入打包隐藏导入后重打安装包。

In a PyInstaller windowed build sys.stdout/sys.stderr are None.

    llama-cpp-python's ``_logger.py`` registers a ctypes log callback at import
    time which calls ``print(..., file=sys.stderr)``. A None stderr inside a C
    callback causes an access-violation on Windows. Redirect missing stdio to
    os.devnull so the callback stays safe.

Replace llama-cpp-python's default log callback with a no-op.

    The default callback (in ``llama_cpp/_logger.py``) does:
        print(text.decode("utf-8"), end="", flush=True, file=sys.stderr)
    Any exception inside this callback (UnicodeDecodeError if the backend
    emits non-UTF-8 bytes; AttributeError if stderr is None) is converted by
    ctypes into ``OSError: access violation reading 0x0000000000000000``.
    A no-op callback eliminates the entire failure class.

    This is the load-bearing defence: the UTF-8 file patch alone is NOT
    enough because the decode happens in Python before the write.

Reopen llama_cpp._utils.{outnull,errnull}_file with UTF-8.

    These files are opened at import time with the system default encoding
    (gbk on Chinese Windows). Even with the no-op log callback installed,
    we still patch them so that any third-party code that bypasses our
    callback and writes directly to them won't trip a UnicodeEncodeError.
Normalize llama.cpp params to avoid values that crash the backend.

Run all three layers of protection. Idempotent and safe to call early.

    Order matters slightly:
      * stdio first (so import of llama_cpp doesn't blow up on None stderr),
      * then no-op callback (replaces default before any backend log fires),
      * then UTF-8 patch (defence in depth for direct writes to devnull).

Clamp ``max_tokens`` so prompt+max_tokens fits ``n_ctx``, and truncate the
    user text if the prompt alone would overflow the context window.

    This is the defence against llama-cpp-python raising
    ``ValueError: Requested tokens (N) exceed context window of M`` when the PO
    text is long and ``local_n_ctx`` is left at its 4096 default. Without it the
    whole batch aborts (the first-PO recipe inference is a cache miss).

One local chat round-trip; returns the raw assistant content.

    Shared by recipe inference and by ``core.ai.data_extract`` so the frozen-app
    crash guards (stdio redirect, no-op log callback, verbose=True) are applied
    in exactly one place. Caller guarantees llama_cpp is importable.
